subtopic: Found money or a lost wallet
passage: Yesterday in the school yard I found a fifty-rupee note near the water tank. My hand closed on it before my mind decided anything. I wanted a mango bar, but I also thought: somebody is missing this. I did not know what to do, so at home I asked Papa. He put down his tea. "Good that you asked, beti. If someone lost it, they will ask the teacher first. Give it to your class teacher in the morning." So today I gave it to Kamal Sir, who announced it in class. Nobody has come yet, but I felt lighter. - Ruchi

qa.q: How much money did Ruchi find?
What was Ruchi feeling as she held the note?
qa.a: Torn, since Ruchi wanted a mango bar but also felt that somebody was missing the money.

qa.q: What else could Ruchi do if nobody claims the note, and why?
qa.a: Ruchi could ask Kamal Sir or the office how it will be handled, so the person who lost it can still claim it.

qa.q: How does Ruchi's father see her question?
qa.a: He is glad she asked, and he helps her think of the teacher as the person the owner would ask first.

grounding: A girl unsure about keeping fifty rupees asks her father, who suggests giving it to the class teacher.

subtopic: Found money or a lost wallet
passage:
Class teacher's note, Class 3, Thursday
This morning Aadhya came to my desk before assembly holding a folded fifty-rupee note. She had found it in the school yard yesterday near the swings. She told me she wasn't sure what to do, so last night she asked her father whether she could keep it. He told her to bring it to school and hand it to me, since someone might report it missing. She did exactly that. I noted the date and place. At lunch a Class 2 girl came to the staffroom in tears; it was her money for the book fair. I returned it to her and told Aadhya. Aadhya smiled for the rest of the day.
- Sangeeta

qa.q: Where did Aadhya find the note?
qa.a: In the school yard near the swings.

qa.q: How did Aadhya feel when she heard the note had found its owner?
qa.a: She felt happy and proud, smiling for the rest of the day.

qa.q: What else could Aadhya do next time she finds something in school?
qa.a: She could hand it straight to the nearest teacher that same day, so the owner gets it back sooner.

qa.q: How does the returned money look to the Class 2 girl?
qa.a: The Class 2 girl, who was in tears, feels hugely relieved to get her book fair money back.

grounding: It shows a girl unsure whether to keep fifty rupees she found in the school yard asking her father, who suggests giving it to the class teacher.

subtopic: Found money or a lost wallet
passage:
Tuesday
Diary, I found fifty rupees in the school yard today, stuck in the grass by the water tap. I didn't know what to do. Is it mine now? I thought about it all the way home. At dinner I asked Papa. He said, "Beta, someone at school probably lost it. Give it to your class teacher tomorrow, in case they come looking." That made sense. Tomorrow I'll give it to Sharmila ma'am first thing. I folded it into my pencil box so it won't get lost again. I feel lighter already, like I'm not carrying a secret.
- Aadhya

qa.q: Where was the fifty rupees stuck?
qa.a: In the grass by the water tap.

qa.q: How did Aadhya feel after talking to Papa?
qa.a: Aadhya felt lighter and relieved, as if no longer carrying a secret.

qa.q: What else could Aadhya do if Sharmila ma'am is absent tomorrow?
qa.a: Aadhya could give it to the school office, so it is still handed to a responsible adult.

qa.q: How might the person who lost the money feel?
qa.a: The person who lost it would feel worried now and very relieved if it turns up with the teacher.

grounding: It shows a child unsure about keeping money found at school asking a parent, who suggests handing it to the class teacher in case someone reports it lost.
